author: Favel Parrett
note: Quotes verified character-for-character against the source text (see recovered-fable-run/REPORT.md). Short extracts for study use.
memoryChain:
A walk through the set, in priority order, as one continuous silly story:

You're in a school cafeteria where MILES, in a lab coat, is weighing single BAKED BEANS on a jeweller's scale (1 - split the food equally). He finishes, then rips a SHARK TOOTH off his own neck like Velcro and buckles it onto HARRY like a coach strapping in a rookie before a match (2 - You can wear this, OK?). Behind them, a SHACK DOOR creaks open and a GAME-SHOW HOST voice booms 'HARRY CURREN, COME ON DOWN!' even though nobody told him Harry was coming (4 - How could that man know his name?). Confused, Harry turns to see gentle SHAMPOO-AD DAD carefully brushing his curls with a tiny doll's hairbrush (5 - Dad even brushed Harry's hair back then) - until Dad suddenly morphs into a COURTROOM LAWYER, jabbing a finger first at a photo on the wall, then double-tapping Harry's chest (7 - because of him. Because of you.). A LOUDSPEAKER bolted to the house behind them blasts four words so loud the night sky cracks like a comic panel (8 - I never wanted you). Then Dad grabs Harry and shakes him like a FLOPPY RAGDOLL pegged to a washing line (9 - shook him like a rag doll). Miles, meanwhile, is SUPERGLUED to the boat's steering wheel with a label-maker on his forehead stamping 'STUCK STUCK STUCK' (10) - and mid-sentence he shrinks into a NAPPY-WEARING BABY on a reef before a giant rubber stamp slams 'NOTHING' over him like a rejected passport (11). Out past the boat, the OCEAN grows an angry cartoon face, steam hissing from its wave-nostrils (12 - the water was angry), and later a giant BLUE HAND rises up and wedgies Miles into the depths (13 - this ocean could hold you down). Cut to young Harry on a beach holding an old shell as his whole body FREEZE-FRAMES, ghost outlines standing around him in the sand (14 - every cell in his body stopped). At the very end, a golden GPS ARROW rises from the last wave, pointing dead certain at a tiny sunny cartoon island (15 - to somewhere warm, to somewhere new), while a LION MADE OF BLACK SEAWATER roars once at the start of the story and once at the end, like a soggy MGM logo (16 - black and cold and roaring). Back in Aunty Jean's hallway, a cupboard box pops open jack-in-the-box style and tiny baby socks float sadly into the air (17 - they were all baby things), while Jean herself stands in the driveway holding a giant red question-mark balloon that inflates every time she repeats her line (18 - what am I meant to do?). And somewhere in George's kitchen, a teacup on the table is quietly printed with MUM'S GHOSTLY FACE, and the whole room goes silent (6 - these are like Mum's cups) - until, at last, Miles lets ONE SINGLE CARTOON TEARDROP fall onto Joe's shoulder, like a dam springing its first tiny leak (3 - he let himself cry).

quotes.quote: Miles was careful to split the food equally
quotes.cue: Beans and mash for dinner, just the two of them - Miles serves Harry's plate first.
quotes.mnemonic: Picture Miles as a lab-coated scientist with a jeweller's scale, weighing two single baked beans against each other so neither brother gets one extra gram.

quotes.cue: The morning Dad forces Harry onto the boat - Miles takes off his own necklace.
quotes.mnemonic: Miles rips the tooth off like a Velcro strap and clips it onto Harry's neck like a coach buckling a rookie's helmet before sending him onto the field.
quotes.sceneTitle: Onto the boat, and the necklace

quotes.cue: Miles with Joe, being told about all the places they'll go.
quotes.mnemonic: A tough action-hero Miles finally lets one single cartoon teardrop go *plink* onto Joe's shoulder, like a dam springing its first tiny leak after years holding firm.

quotes.quote: How could that man know his name?
quotes.cue: Harry bolts from George Fuller's shack - a stranger calls him by name.
quotes.mnemonic: A shack door creaks open and a booming game-show-host voice bellows 'HARRY CURREN, COME ON DOWN!' - except Harry never told a single soul he was there.
quotes.sceneTitle: No one home, and the shack

quotes.quote: Dad even brushed Harry’s hair back then
quotes.cue: Miles remembers what Dad used to be like, in the same memory as Mum and the lucky curls.
quotes.mnemonic: Picture gentle past-Dad in a shampoo advert, carefully brushing Harry's curls with a tiny doll's hairbrush - the exact opposite of the Dad who shakes Harry later.

quotes.cue: Harry drinking tea at George's place after Dad's beating - he notices the cups.
quotes.mnemonic: Harry lifts a teacup at George's table and it's printed with Mum's ghostly face - and the whole room goes dead silent.
quotes.sceneTitle: George, a cloth, and a bottle

quotes.quote: because of him. Because of you.
quotes.cue: Dad, holding the tooth, tells Miles why their mother was leaving.
quotes.mnemonic: Dad jabs a finger first at a photo of Uncle Nick, then swivels and double-taps Harry's chest, like a courtroom lawyer pointing at two suspects in a row.
quotes.sceneTitle: The air pump, and because of you

quotes.cue: Dad's voice through the walls as the boys flee into the scrub.
quotes.mnemonic: A giant loudspeaker bolted to the house wall blasts these four words so loud the night sky visibly cracks open like a comic-book sound effect.

quotes.quote: shook him like a rag doll
quotes.cue: Dad grabs Harry after he uses the radio in protected waters.
quotes.mnemonic: Dad grabs Harry and shakes him exactly like a floppy ragdoll pegged to a washing line - arms and legs flapping like wet spaghetti.
quotes.sceneTitle: The air pump, and because of you

quotes.quote: Stuck working for Dad, stuck being responsible for Harry
quotes.cue: Miles on the cliff, after Joe warns him he'll get stuck.
quotes.mnemonic: Miles is superglued to the boat's steering wheel, a label-maker stuck to his forehead endlessly printing 'STUCK STUCK STUCK STUCK.'

quotes.quote: He was just a kid. A baby. He was nothing.
quotes.cue: Miles, moments before the 'stuck' line, thinking about how outmatched he is.
quotes.mnemonic: Mid-sentence, Miles shrinks into a nappy-wearing baby standing on a giant reef, then a rubber stamp slams down the word 'NOTHING' over him like a rejected passport.

quotes.cue: Dawn on Dad's boat off Bruny - Miles reads the surface for danger.
quotes.mnemonic: The ocean grows a scrunched-up cartoon face with steam hissing from wave-shaped nostrils, shaking an angry fist-wave at Miles's little boat.
quotes.sceneTitle: Uncle Nick and the empty dinghy

quotes.quote: This ocean could hold you down
quotes.cue: Miles swimming out to Harry in the huge swell after the boat capsizes.
quotes.mnemonic: A giant blue hand rises out of the sea and presses down on Miles's head like a schoolyard bully doing a wedgie - except the bully is the entire Tasman Sea.

quotes.quote: every cell in his body stopped
quotes.cue: Harry alone on the beach at Cloudy Bay, holding an old abalone shell.
quotes.core: every cell in his body stopped
quotes.mnemonic: Harry holds an ancient abalone shell and his whole body freeze-frames like a paused video, faint ghost outlines of long-dead people standing around him on the sand.

quotes.quote: To somewhere warm. To somewhere new.
quotes.cue: The final two lines of the novel, right after George returns the tooth.
quotes.mnemonic: A glowing golden GPS arrow rises out of the final wave and points, dead certain, straight at a tiny sunny cartoon island in the distance.

quotes.cue: The very first line of the novel, describing the dark water past the shallows (also echoed on the last page).
quotes.mnemonic: A lion made of black seawater roars once at the very start of the book and once at the very end - like the MGM lion, but soaking wet and terrifying.

quotes.cue: Miles finds a box in Aunty Jean's cupboard while she cuts his hair.
quotes.mnemonic: Aunty Jean's cupboard box pops open like a jack-in-the-box, but instead of a clown, tiny baby socks and blankets spring out and float sadly around the room.

quotes.quote: What am I meant to do? What am I meant to do?
quotes.cue: Aunty Jean, in the same scene, talking about selling Granddad's house.
quotes.core: What am I meant to do?
quotes.mnemonic: Aunty Jean stands in the driveway holding a giant red question-mark balloon, and it visibly inflates bigger each time she repeats the line.
